_meta.description: Golden callee (outbound) dataset for direct-callee recall benchmarking
_meta.usage: Run scripts/benchmark/run_caller_recall.sh run --project-path ... --direction callees to evaluate
_meta.normalization: Chunk IDs normalized (line ranges stripped via evaluation/metrics.py:normalize_chunk_id)
_meta.format: target_chunk_id → list of expected direct-callee chunk IDs
_meta.relevance_scale: All entries in expected_callees are grade=2 (direct callee confirmed by code reading)

queries.description: run_resolvers calls prepare_scoped_files and wrap_in_context directly; resolver.available()/.resolve() are Protocol-dispatched (never chunked as separate targets) and dict.get() fans out ambiguously via AST bare-name matching -- both excluded from expected_callees as known AST fan-out, not genuine misses

PyanResolver.resolve calls prepare_scoped_files, the shared gather/scope/validate preamble extracted for PyanResolver, LibCSTResolver, and LSPResolver. gather_py_files, scope_to_indexed_files, and validate_py_files are now called from inside prepare_scoped_files (2-hop), not directly from resolve

inject_call_edges (module-level function in search/call_edge_injection.py) calls run_resolvers and storage.upgrade_call_edge (2026-09-02 repair: the target was IndexWriteStage.inject_call_edges, which no longer contains these calls and only delegates here; the function is >100 lines so the index stores it as split_block fragments that normalize to the method: form)

scope_to_indexed_files calls Path(fn).resolve().relative_to(project_root); .resolve() is not in graph_integration.py's _COMMON_METHODS denylist, so the AST resolver fans it out ambiguously to every *.resolve chunk in the project. These are known false positives, not scored against expected_callees (which stays [] -- there are no genuine project-internal callees here).
